Capital One.

Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Three taxpayer-funded ads promoting President Trump
ahead of the midterm elections
have cost about one and a half million dollars,
according to Ad Impact.
The White House defends them as public service announcements,
but the ads are attracting mounting criticism.
Senate Republican Majority Leader John Thune told reporters
that taxpayer dollars shouldn't pay for the ads.
Some legal experts say they run afoul of federal laws
against using public funds for propaganda.
A second deputy FBI director is leaving the bureau
after just over a year in the job.
The news comes after his co-director resigned in early January.
NPR's Ryan Lucas reports.
Andrew Bailey says in a post on X
that he is stepping down to return to his family in Missouri.
But he says he's confident that Director Cash Patel
will continue the work,
including reforming the FBI and combating violent crime.
Patel thanked Bailey for his service on X as well.
Bailey, a former attorney general for the state of Missouri,
joined the FBI last August under an unusual arrangement
as co-deputy director alongside Dan Bongino,
a right-wing former podcast host.
Bongino left the bureau in January.
Now Bailey, too, is departing.
It's unclear whether he will be replaced.
The current remaining deputy director
is a career special agent,
which was the norm until the second Trump administration.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
-The Trump administration is relaxing requirements
for automakers to control pollution
from gasoline-powered cars and light trucks.
The new standards set the average for these vehicles
at roughly 35 miles per gallon in 2031 model year,
down from a projected 50.4 miles per gallon
under rules put in place by the Biden administration.
President Trump claims these less stringent mileage
requirements would save Americans
thousands of dollars on a new car.
A New York prosecutor has reopened an investigation
into gang rape allegations at a Cornell University fraternity
in response to a lawsuit.
The complaint was filed by a woman
who says she was sexually assaulted in 2024 by seven students
after being plied with alcohol and drugs,
and PR's Brian Mann reports.
-In her civil lawsuit filed this month,
the woman identified as Jane Doe describes a brutal assault.
She wasn't old enough to drink legally
but said she was pressured at a Ki-5 fraternity party
to use alcohol and drugs.
She describes them being gang-raped,
often while she was incapacitated over a period of hours.
The lawsuit filing includes a screen capture
of Snapchat messages between some of the men
where they appear to joke and invite others to take part.
This lawsuit also accuses Cornell University
of failing to properly respond to the alleged violence.
I should say we don't know exactly what actions
Cornell took against these individuals.
The university said some were suspended or expelled.
-NPR's Brian Mann reporting.
U.S. stocks pulled further from their record highs today.
The S&P 500 fell three-quarters of a percent.
This is NPR News.
NVIDIA has unveiled a new security platform
that it says is designed to prevent
AI agents from going rogue.
The platform includes software
that sets boundaries for AI agents.
This comes after recent incidents of AI models
escaping and breaking into other organizations.
Business leaders and elected officials
in Jackson Hole, Wyoming are urging the Secretary
of the Interior to say no to a baseball field
inside Grand Teton National Park.
KHOL Jackson's Sophia Boyd Fleagle reports.
-Some Jackson Hole locals were shocked
by a recent Washington Post report
that the Trump administration had scouted locations
in Grand Teton National Park to build a baseball park
to host a major league baseball game.
NPR has not independently confirmed the report.
Rick Howe is a longtime leader
of the Jackson Hole Chamber of Commerce.
-I thought it was just kind of one
of those conspiracy theories of jokes.
It isn't.
This isn't something we should be accepting.
-How told commissioners that even a temporary field
on already disturbed land
would undermine the purpose of the park
to protect its natural resources, wildlife,
and serve the public.
Commissioners immediately signed onto a chamber letter
asking the Interior Department to reject the proposal
and direct any other commercial events
to venues that aren't protected.
For NPR News, I'm Sophia Boyd Fleagle in Jackson.
-SpaceX has launched its enormous starship into orbit
for the first time and successfully delivered
the newest and most advanced star links yet,
but flight controllers brought the spacecraft back to Earth
instead of making six full laps around Earth as originally planned,
the company's trying to prove the rocket's readiness
for NASA's Artemis Moon program.
